If a company identifies a seasonal pattern in their sales data, how should this influence their inventory management strategy?
options: Increase inventory levels uniformly throughout the year to avoid any potential stockouts.
Adjust inventory levels based on historical sales data to match the anticipated seasonal demand.
Reduce inventory levels during peak seasons to minimize holding costs.
Keep inventory levels constant, ignoring seasonal trends to simplify logistics.
questions.correct_answer: Adjust inventory levels based on historical sales data to match the anticipated seasonal demand.

questions.text: Which of the following statements best describes the difference between platform companies and niche companies?
options: Platform companies focus on creating a broad ecosystem where multiple users, services, or businesses can interact, while niche companies specialize in a specific product or service aimed at a particular market segment.
Platform companies usually operate in small markets with specialized audiences, whereas niche companies dominate large, general markets with diverse customer bases.
Platform companies rely solely on physical products for revenue, whereas niche companies generate income primarily through digital services.
Platform companies are less scalable than niche companies because they target a smaller audience, while niche companies can easily expand to a broader market.
questions.correct_answer: Platform companies focus on creating a broad ecosystem where multiple users, services, or businesses can interact, while niche companies specialize in a specific product or service aimed at a particular market segment.

questions.text: Which of the following best explains the risk of maintaining excessively low Days of Inventory?
options: It increases working capital efficiency and production stability.
It may lead to stockouts, production stoppages, and missed sales opportunities.
It reduces supplier dependency and improves forecasting accuracy.
It helps maintain a buffer against market fluctuations.
correct_answer: It may lead to stockouts, production stoppages, and missed sales opportunities.
questions.comprehension_passage: In recent months, Trio Engineering Pvt. Ltd., a mid-sized automotive components manufacturer, has reported an unusually low level of inventory on hand. The Days of Inventory (DOI) has fallen sharply below the company’s usual level. At first, management viewed this as a sign of lean and efficient operations. However, within a few weeks, the production department began facing frequent raw material shortages, leading to idle machine hours, delayed deliveries, and unmet customer orders. The procurement team revealed that the company had been implementing an aggressive cost- control drive to reduce inventory-carrying costs. Suppliers were also asked to deliver materials just-in-time. But due to transportation delays and sudden demand surges, low DOI became common.

questions.text: Which of the following corrective actions should Trio Engineering consider restoring balance between efficiency and reliability?
options: Establish minimum safety stock levels for critical raw materials.
Strengthen demand forecasting using sales and market data.
Negotiate longer supplier credit periods instead of inventory cuts.
Review supplier performance and delivery reliability.
Reduce re-order levels further to maintain low inventory costs.
correct_answer: Establish minimum safety stock levels for critical raw materials.
Strengthen demand forecasting using sales and market data.
Review supplier performance and delivery reliability.

questions.text: Which category does ProMech Components Ltd. fall into?
questions.comprehension_passage: During the month of July, the operations team at ProMech Components Ltd., a manufacturer of automotive assemblies, observed that the total output from their main assembly line had declined compared to previous months. Although the production schedule remained unchanged, managers suspected that frequent stoppages and slower production rates might be affecting efficiency. A review of the production records revealed that the line had been scheduled to operate for 400 hours in July. However, around 80 hours were lost due to setup adjustments, maintenance delays, and minor breakdowns, leaving less time for productive operation. Under ideal conditions, the line is capable of producing 200 components per hour, but during the month, the average operating rate dropped to about 150 components per hour. By the end of July, the plant had assembled 45,000 units, out of which roughly 2,250 failed to pass the final quality inspection. The management then evaluates how efficiently the assembly line was utilized by estimating its Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) — an integrated measure of availability, performance, and quality. The international benchmarks are then Interpreted based on the OEE value using the following categorization ● World Class → ≥ 85% ● Industry Average → 60–85% ● Below Average → 40–60% ● Underperforming → < 40%

An analyst builds a Pivot Table to summarize quarterly sales by region. After adding new March data to the source sheet, totals in the Pivot remain unchanged. Why?
options: Pivot Tables auto-refresh when new data is added.
Source data range must be updated or refreshed manually.
The new data used a different number format.
The Pivot Table cannot be altered once created.
questions.correct_answer: Source data range must be updated or refreshed manually.
